findings.finding: The cited SC-4 test does not verify the criterion's REJECT outcome. SC-4 requires that a model-reported defect produces a REJECT verdict carrying the finding and evidence verbatim. The cited test calls only `judge()` and asserts on the returned `Judgment` (`defect_found` and `findings`). It never runs `validate()` and never checks for a `Reject`. If the gate failed to turn a defect judgment into a `Reject`, or dropped or rewrote the findings when building it, this test would still pass. The `test_gate.py` file shown has no test where the fake provider reports a defect, so no cited test covers the defect-to-REJECT step. I only see the tests shown; if a gate-level defect test exists elsewhere, it is not cited.
findings.evidence: The SC-4 test docstring describes only Judgment-level behaviour ('arrive in the Judgment untouched'), and its assertions stop at the Judgment object. In `test_gate.py` the fake provider always returns `{"defect_found": False, "findings": []}`, and no test exercises the defect-to-Reject path.

findings.finding: The SC-3 test does not verify two parts of the criterion: that the PR body carries the task id, and that `Satisfies:` names exactly the task's criteria. The task id is asserted only against the PR title, not the body. The Satisfies check is a substring match, so extra trailing criteria would still pass.
findings.evidence: SC-3 requires a PR whose body carries the task id and `Satisfies:` naming exactly the task's criteria. The test extracts `body` but only checks the title for "T-1". If `_pr_body` dropped the task id, the test would still pass, because the title is built separately in `_pr_title`. The Satisfies assertion `"Satisfies: SC-1, SC-2" in body` is a prefix/substring check, so a body reading `Satisfies: SC-1, SC-2, SC-3` would also pass despite claiming more than the task's criteria. The fixture's criteria list is in `test_brief` and is not shown, so I cannot say whether the fixture has other criteria. The test still does not pin the line to exactly the task's criteria. The implementation appears to do the right thing; the weakness is in the test's ability to catch a regression.

findings.finding: SC-2 requires a fixture for each rule branch, but the "Next task <id> of <spec>" branch of `next_action` is never asserted. In `test_sc2_next_action_precedence` the Approved spec `tasked` with an open task is added after the compact spec `compact`. Compact wins on slug order, so the "Next task" branch never fires. No other cited test asserts that branch either. If that branch were broken or removed, every cited SC-2 test would still pass. I did not see the spec's Approach text, so I can't confirm the exact list of rule branches. This one is plainly a branch in `next_action`.
findings.evidence: The only assertions touching the tasked spec are the slug-order check and the escalation-file check, neither of which exercises the task branch. The SC-1 fixture has `alpha` Approved with open task T-2, but that test never checks the next action text.

findings.finding: SC-4 requires that when the model reports a defect, the verdict is `REJECT` carrying the model's finding and evidence verbatim. The cited test only exercises `judge()` and asserts on the returned `Judgment`. It never builds a `Reject` verdict and never goes through `validate()`. If the gate dropped, altered or failed to convert a model-reported defect into a `Reject`, this test would still pass.
findings.evidence: The cited SC-4 test ends with assertions on `judgment.defect_found` and `judgment.findings`, with no verdict-level assertion. `test_gate.py` is the only place `validate()` is exercised. Its four tests (SC-1, SC-2, SC-3, SC-7) all use a fake provider that returns `defect_found: False`, so no shown test drives a model-reported defect through the gate to a `Reject`. The gate code itself is not in the diff, so I cannot say whether another test covers this. Nothing cited does.

findings.finding: The cited SC-4 test checks only that judge() returns the model's finding and evidence unchanged in a Judgment object. SC-4 says the verdict is REJECT carrying that finding and evidence. The test never calls validate() and never asserts a Reject verdict. If the gate turned a defect judgment into a Pass, or dropped the findings from the Reject, this test would still pass. findings.evidence: The criterion requires a REJECT verdict. The cited test's assertions are limited to `judgment.defect_found is True` and `judgment.findings == (Finding(...),)`. The test_judgment.py docstring itself scopes the test to the judgment stage ('carried into the judgment verbatim'), not the verdict. The Traceability table still maps SC-4 to this test unchanged.
